q1_manage_gate_semantics.rule: The manage-gate settings module shall be the exact historical revision's repository-authored pytest Django settings module (the settings module the repository itself authors for its pytest workload, i.e. the repo pytest --ds / DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE-for-tests value), resolved from the exact materialized worktree. The manage check command is: python manage.py check --settings=<repo-authored pytest settings module>.
q1_manage_gate_semantics.why_not_merely_unit56_fix: Candidate C is the faithful generalization of the frozen D7 R3 smoke semantics (manage gate runs against the repository's TEST settings module) to the full population. For 218 commits the repo-authored pytest settings module IS saleor.tests.settings (effective command byte-identical to current). For the single legacy commit 8220a534... the repository authors tests.settings, which exists in its exact tree. The same general repository/semantics-based rule handles both; it is not keyed to task/commit/unit identity.

q2_test_settings_vs_default.ruling: Manage-gate semantics intentionally use the repository-authored TEST (pytest) settings module, NOT the repository's normal manage.py default settings (saleor.settings).
evidence: Frozen D7 R3 harness contract (research/env-canon-evidence/d7-r3/harness/D7_R3_HARNESS_CONTRACT.md, section F Smoke) preserves the manage smoke gate as `manage.py check --settings=saleor.tests.settings` — the manage gate is frozen against the repository's TEST settings module, not against manage.py's default.

The manage.py default is `saleor.settings` in BOTH signatures (Phase-1 signatures JSON); the frozen R3 smoke semantics deliberately overrides it with the test settings module. The audit flagged this as 'a deliberate semantic override that Phase 2 should confirm is intended' (R4_FRAMEWORK_SEMANTICS_AUDIT_144.md section 9). This decision confirms it is intended.

The manage gate is a framework gate: it verifies the installed environment can run Django system checks under the same settings configuration the repository's own test suite (pytest) uses. The pytest gate already inherits the repo --ds config; the manage gate validating the same repo-authored test settings module is the semantically consistent framework check.

Using manage.py's default (saleor.settings) would change the effective framework-gate command for ALL 143 matching units (to `python manage.py check` without --settings) and would not reflect the settings under which the workload's tests actually run.

manage_vs_pytest_decoupled.explanation: Manage and pytest semantics remain intentionally decoupled at the mechanism level. The manage gate FORCES the settings module explicitly via --settings; the pytest gate INHERITS the repository-authored config (--ds) without forcing. Under Candidate C both resolve to the SAME repository-authored settings module (saleor.tests.settings for the modern signature, tests.settings for the legacy signature), so they are semantically consistent while remaining mechanically decoupled. Neither gate is merged into the other.
